Jamie Overton to Janith Liyanage, no run, much needed dot ball for England. Full and quick outside off, Janith Liyanage goes for a flashy drive, and gets beaten. Taken by the keeper at chest height, good amount of carry
Jamie Overton to Janith Liyanage, 1 run, that was full and quick on middle and leg, drilled to long-on by Janith Liyanage for a single
Josh Tongue [8.0-1-71-1] is back into the attack
Josh Tongue to Janith Liyanage, 1 run, on the shorter side, a slower one, Janith Liyanage pulls it towards deep mid-wicket for a single
Josh Tongue to Dunith Wellalage, THATS OUT!! Bowled!!

Josh Tongue to Dunith Wellalage, out Bowled!! Is there a twist in the tale? Pitched up by the bowler from round the wicket, hint of swing, Dunith Wellalage goes for a wild swing, misses it altogether, as the middle and leg stumps goes for a toss. Looked like an ugly slog, and the batsman has to pay the price for it. This match is going right down the wire. All three results still possible. England can win, Sri Lanka can win, and there's a chance of a Super over as well. Dunith Wellalage b Josh Tongue 8(7) [4s-1]
Eshan Malinga, left handed bat, comes to the crease
Josh Tongue to Eshan Malinga, THATS OUT!! Bowled!!

Josh Tongue to Eshan Malinga, out Bowled!! Two in two for Josh Tongue. He's on a hat-trick. Full and quick from round the wicket, Eshan Malinga goes for a straight drive, plays down the wrong line, and the middle stump has been uprooted. 7 runs needed in 3 balls. They need Liyanage to get back on strike. Eshan Malinga b Josh Tongue 0(1)
Asitha Fernando, right handed bat, comes to the crease

Josh Tongue to Asitha Fernando, 1 run, no hat-trick for Josh Tongue. And Liyanage is back on strike. Width on offer outside off, Asitha Fernando slashes away from his body, gets an outside edge towards third man. A fumble in the deep, but they stick to a single. 6 runs needed in 2 balls

Josh Tongue to Janith Liyanage, SIX, Janith Liyanage does the unthinkable. Second ever highest run chase in ODIs. Sri Lanka's highest ODI run chase! The Sri Lankan players charge on to the field and hug Janith Liyanage. They lost two wickets in the final over, but he has thumped this over long-off to seal the fate of his match. Such a crucial strike under pressure. Pitched up the bowler around off, right into the slot, and Janith Liyanage smokes it over the boundary to pull it off

Pavan Rathnayake | Player of the Match: Very happy. Important win for our team. [What was the conversation like?] So we think wicket was very good. So we back our normal game, that's it. [On the partnerships] Yeah, very good team game. I think every partnership played very well. [You think this 100 is the best so far?] Yeah, this one. Hundred percent.

Harry Brook | England captain: [What did you make of the game?] Incredible game of cricket. I thought both teams were exceptional. Sri Lanka just outplayed us, unfortunately. We couldn't quite hit our straps with the ball and played into their strengths a little bit, and again they played exceptional cricket to knock off 400. I think you said first time in 20 years is an incredible achievement, so fair play to them. [On his knock] Yeah, it's nice to things. Unfortunately, it doesn't mean anything now, being on the losing side. It has no value whatsoever in my eyes. [Tougher conversations ahead?] Yeah, we've got to go back to the drawing board a little bit. No, we know where we've gone wrong. Unfortunately, we didn't execute well enough with the ball. We've got a great opportunity in the next couple of games to try and nail down a spot in the final. And yeah, we've got to go back to keeping things simple and backing ourselves and pick our chins up and go again next game.

That brings us to the end of today’s coverage! Harry Brook stole the spotlight in the first innings, smashing his maiden ODI double century to propel England to their highest-ever total in the format. However, Sri Lanka responded with an even more remarkable effort, producing their highest-ever ODI total and pulling off the second-highest successful run chase in ODI history. It was a truly memorable contest. All eyes will now be on England as they look to bounce back when they face Pakistan in Lahore in their next outing. Goodbye and take care!
